crime: Every evening until lockup, the girl reads in the library beneath the unwilting cherry tree, and she never takes {WITCH_NAME}'s ribbon out of her hair. Every night at half past nine, {WITCH_NAME} sits in the lounge and calls the ribbon home. It slips out of the girl's hair and flies to her hand, and the moment it leaves, the girl comes down to join her.
One evening after supper, in the library, the girl unties the ribbon and holds it out with a smile. "Say no to me once. Or take it back, and stop fetching me."
The first time {WITCH_NAME} ever said no, her aunt set her packed suitcase by the front door. "One more no, and you go out this door." She has not said no since.

She closes both hands around the girl's throat until the girl goes still, her outstretched hand still holding the ribbon. {WITCH_NAME} takes it from those fingers and hangs it on a tree in the courtyard. From eight o'clock she sits among the other prisoners in the lounge, and she stays there until the body is found. At half past nine, as she does every night, she calls her ribbon home. In front of them all, it streaks in from the rainy courtyard and lands dripping in her palm.

In the trial court, the prisoners take it that the girl was out in the rain at half past nine and was killed after coming back in, while {WITCH_NAME} sat among them. Then the prisoner who found the body in the library remembers lifting the girl's head from beneath the unwilting cherry tree: her hair and uniform were bone dry. The prisoners understand. The girl never went out. Only the ribbon hung in the rain, without her, until its owner called it in.
fields.epitaph: She never said no again, except once, with both hands, to the one girl who asked to hear it.
fields.epithet: A Yes Packed by the Door
execution: The execution stand opens a huge iron suitcase and chains her inside, curled up, with one open palm raised above the rim. The lid lowers onto her raised palm and shuts. The buckles snap closed one by one. The stand sets the buckled suitcase upright beside the entrance of the trial court, like luggage waiting to be sent out. From inside, she knocks. The knocks come slower, and then not at all. No one comes to open it.

magic.name: Come Home
magic.text: She can call anything she has ever held flying back into her open palm, however far or hidden.
